note: Director cycle 1: planner writes the overview.

question: [data model] What is a system?

options.label: A copy of a network type ("Supply Air 2"), as `duplicateNetworkType` does (`scene.ts:2401`).
A new stored entity with a name and service keys, in `ProjectDocument.systems`.
A name on a calculated network, found by its start point.

reason: A mixes two meanings. The copy also changes the look of the type, and a type cannot hold rooms or a start point. C does not exist before a segment is drawn, so it cannot serve routing. B keeps the network type of the segment as the only network type. A system never writes on a segment. So the rule "the segment defines the network type" and the cascade stay true. Precedent: `Panel` (`circuit.ts:72`).

question: [data model] How does the user give rooms to a system, and what happens when the user runs Detect rooms again?

options.label: Pick rooms. The link is `Room.systems`. A change of the link locks the room (like `roomTypeSource: 'user'`). Side effect: `updateRoom` locks a room only for the fields that it lists (`room.ts:165`-`:168`). A locked room keeps its old polygon when Detect rooms runs again, and the new polygon of that room is dropped (`room.ts:190`-`:192`). The user loses a better outline.

Pick rooms. The link does not lock the room. When Detect rooms replaces a room, the new room takes `systems` from the old room if the label point of the new room lies inside the old polygon. This is the same test that `mergeDetectedRooms` uses to drop a duplicate (`room.ts:197`-`:198`). `roomPlacementKey` (`placement-layout.ts:829`) is not a good match key here: it includes the polygon, so it c...
Draw zones (polygons) and store them.
Free text in `Room.properties` (`room.ts:36`).

reason: it uses the rooms that exist and has no side effect on the polygon. A is simple but the lock blocks a better outline. C is a new entity and a new tool. D is free text, so a rename of a system breaks the link. B needs one change in `mergeDetectedRooms` and a core test. Both A and B need the clean-up of dangling ids on load (see section 3).

question: [data model] Is a floor (a PDF page) a zone? What happens with a multi-page PDF?

options.label: No. Stamps are not page-scoped (G1). One PDF file is one floor. The user uses one PDF file for each floor. When the PDF has more than one page (`getPageCount()`, `packages/pdf-engine/src/index.ts:128`), the system lookup is off and the Systems panel says so. Every port uses its implicit system. The app does not guess.
Yes. Add `pageIndex` to `PlacedStamp` and filter by page. Schema 19. The status bar count also filters by page.

reason: B is a large change that no routing part needs if the user keeps one floor in each file. A refusal is better than a wrong system: a stamp on page 2 would be looked up in the rooms of page 1. Not verified: how many users keep several floors in one multi-page PDF. If the user does, answer B and R2 gains one phase. The R2 plan has a test: a core test with rooms on two pages, and a browser check with a real multi-page PDF. Not verified: whether `fixtures/pdfs/` has a multi-page PDF. If none, the tester reports NEEDS_CONTEXT. Nobody makes a fake PDF.

question: [data model] Can a system serve more than one PDF file (a riser)?

options.label: No. A system lives in one document. A riser is a start point (R3) on each floor.
Yes. Add a project level above the documents.

reason: there is no project level (`scene.ts:624`). B changes the save format and the open flow. R3 can still draw one riser stub on each floor.

question: [data model] Does one system serve more than one network type (supply and return of one unit)?

options.label: Yes. One system lists several service keys ("AHU 1": `supply-air`, `return-air`). When the user picks AHU 1 for a room, the app sets the link for every key of AHU 1. The user can then set one key to another system (exhaust to "Exhaust fan 3").
Two linked systems (one for supply, one for return).
Two independent systems.

reason: the user picks the rooms once, not twice, and can still split one type. `Room.systems` is a map, so a room can never have two systems for one key. This removes the "two systems list the same type" conflict by construction.

question: Does a hand-placed stamp get the system of the room under it?

options.label: Yes, calculated from the position with `roomsAtPoint` on the shown page (see the rule above). Nothing is stored on the stamp. If the user moves the stamp, the system follows.
Also allow a per-port override on the stamp (`PlacedStamp.routingSystems`). [data model]

reason: it makes Auto-place and a hand-placed stamp behave the same. Moved and unmoved stamps follow a change of the room link with no rewrite. B can come later with no change of A.

question: [data model] Is the list of systems part of the undo history?

options.label: Yes. Add `systems: Record<string, System>` to `DrawingState` (`packages/render/src/document.ts:29`-`:40`), like `panels` and `circuits`, which are undo-tracked (`document.ts:34`-`:37`).

No. A plain list on the document, like `networkTypes`, `terminalCapacities` and `portGroups` (`document.ts:34` comment, `:128`-`:151`). Undo of a room link can then name a system that the user deleted. The lookup treats such an id as "no system".

reason: `Room.systems` is undo-tracked, because rooms are (`document.ts:38`). A list that is not tracked gives a dangling id after one undo. A costs one more record in `DrawingState` and a command for add, rename and delete. The delete command also removes the room links in the same undo step.

question: [data model] What is a start point?

options.label: An equipment stamp and its ports (`System.startStampId`, `startPortIds`) for a mechanical system. A shaft is an equipment stamp drawn in the shaft room.
A new fitting kind `riser`.
The shaft room itself.

reason: the flow solve already starts at an equipment stamp (`flow.ts:95`). Not verified: whether the stamp library has a shaft stamp. If it does not, R3 adds one library stamp, and that stays inside the Custom stamp library work. An electrical system does not use this field (see D-R7-01).

question: A port group can join a supply run and a return run into one network (G7). What does R3 do?

options.label: `computeNetworks` stops joining runs of different network types through a group. The group still joins runs of one type.
Leave it. Routing treats each port alone.

reason: the run of one network type must not take the type of another (rule 2). `computeNetworks` today gives a network the type of the first segment of the union (`network.ts:140`-`:165`). B leaves a wrong cascade. The change is small. The R3 plan lists every consumer and tests each:

question: [data model] Where does the route area come from?

options.label: Automatic only, from the rooms of type Corridor and Shaft.
Automatic, and the user can draw route zones and "no crossing" lines by hand (stored).
Hand-drawn only.

reason: room types come from name matching and can be wrong (`room.ts:39`, `roomTypeSource: 'matched'`). The user needs a way to fix it. The user also needs a way to mark a fire-compartment wall that no branch may cross (M7). The plan puts A first and the hand items in a later phase. A stored zone is a polygon and a page index. A stored "no crossing" line is a line and a page index.

question: Is a 2D draft acceptable for R4 and R6 (G13)?

options.label: Yes. The route has no height. The app shows a note: "Draft in 2D. Check clashes and clearances yourself." The designer decides heights and clashes.
First add a height (elevation) to a segment, then route in 3 steps. This is a per-segment field, so it needs a cascade check (rule 2) and a larger model.

reason: MepApp has no height model and no obstacle model today. B is a separate large feature. A gives value now and does not block B later.

question: [data model] What is the unit of the flow?

options.label: dm³/s inside, for every type. The UI shows dm³/s, with m³/h as a display option (1 dm³/s = 3.6 m³/h). The library labels change from CFM and GPM to dm³/s.
Keep the labels and convert at the edge.
A unit on each network type with a conversion table.

reason: the air demands already use dm³/s (`room-need.ts:27`-`:28`). `NetworkType.units` is a free label that no code reads (`network.ts:26`). One unit means no conversion bug. An old drawing keeps its old label text. This covers air only. Water follows D-R5-05. Not verified: where the display option is stored (the user preferences or the file).

question: Which sizing method?

options.label: Each network type has two limits: a maximum velocity (m/s) and a maximum pressure drop (Pa/m). The size is the smallest standard size that meets both. Equal friction for ducts, velocity plus Pa/m for pipes.
Maximum velocity only.
Equal friction only.

reason: it is the common practice, and it never gives a size that fails one limit. The limit values and the size tables come from the standards. The tables are "read from the standard in R5, not from memory": the EN 1506 table of round duct sizes (13 or 14 sizes, not verified), the EN 1505 steps for rectangular ducts, and the DN series for pipes. The R5 research task reads them first.

question: [data model] Where are the sizing settings stored?

options.label: Optional fields on `NetworkType`: maximum velocity, maximum Pa/m, size series, and the delta T of D-R5-05 (the drawing copy, so they travel with the file and follow the adoption path).
A separate list `sizingRules` by network type id on the document.

reason: reuse. The drawing already keeps its own copy of each type. B is a second place to read for one type.

question: [data model] How does a stamp with two flows keep them (G5)?

options.label: Keep one number. R5 sizes only terminals with one flow.
Add `PlacedStamp.portCapacities` (port id to number). `terminalCapacities` stays for a stamp with one flow.

reason: a fan coil unit has a heating flow and a cooling flow on two ports. It also has an air flow, and a condensate drain. A would size one of them wrong. R5 v1 sizes the water ports. The air flow and the drain of a fan coil unit stay outside R5 v1 and the plan says so. Not verified: how Auto-place gives such a stamp two flows. Today a rule serves one demand type, so the plan adds the entry by hand in Properties first.

question: [data model] How does R5 turn a heating or cooling power in W into a water flow (G16)?

options.label: R5 v1 sizes air networks only. Water networks wait for a later version.

R5 v1 also sizes water. The flow is q = P / (cp × delta T). Each water network type gets a delta T field (D-R5-03). The fluid is water. R5 asks for the delta T when the field is empty. The plan gives no default value. Typical values (for example 20 K for heating and 6 K for cooling) are not verified.

reason: the batch D-R5-03 already adds fields to `NetworkType`, so one more field is cheap. A leaves out heating and cooling, which are half of the HVAC work. The user enters delta T, so the app invents no value. R5 reads cp of water from a source and states it in the plan. Not verified: the source value.

question: One branch for each terminal or for each room?

options.label: For each terminal, from the nearest point of the main.
For each room: one branch to the room, then sub-branches to its terminals.

reason: this is how designers draw it. It gives fewer crossings and a clean tee at the room.

question: [data model] What does a re-run do with routed segments?

options.label: Mark routed segments (`Segment.routedBy`). A re-run replaces unchanged routed segments and keeps hand-drawn or edited ones. This is the same idea as `autoPlaced.moved` (`stamp.ts:27`).
A re-run only connects open ports and never removes a segment.
A re-run removes all routed segments.

reason: it matches Auto-place, so the user learns one rule. The new field says how the segment was made. It does not say what network the segment is on, so rule 2 stays true.

question: [data model] Which panel serves which rooms?

options.label: An electrical system of R2 (service key `electrical`). Rooms link to it through `Room.systems['electrical']`. The system has `panelId`. `Panel.equipmentStampId` (`circuit.ts:75`) is the only source of the panel stamp. The system stores no start stamp, and R7 reads no field of R3. A terminal without a routing target (Light, Sockets) uses the electrical system of its room.
A list of rooms on `Panel`.
The nearest panel by distance, with no stored link.

reason: one model for rooms and services, and one source for the panel stamp (rule 3). R7 needs R2 only. If the user answers D-R2-01 with A or C, this becomes B.

question: [data model] Where are the circuit limits, and what are they?

options.label: Reuse `CircuitType.defaultCapacity` (`circuit.ts:99`) as the load limit in `units`, and add optional `maxTerminals` and `diversity` (for sockets) on `CircuitType`. The document already has its own copy of the circuit types (`project.ts:38`).
New fields only. `defaultCapacity` keeps its unused meaning.
Fixed values in code.

reason: reuse (rule 3). `defaultCapacity` is already a number in W that the user edits for each type, and nothing reads it. All limits are user-editable defaults with the source "design practice". NEN 1010:2020 no longer regulates a minimum or maximum count of sockets or luminaires per circuit, and IEC 60364 does not set it either. The real protection is the rating of the breaker and the section of the cable. Source: Techniek Nederland, webinar NEN 1010:2020 (https://technieknederland.nl/stream/presentatie-webinar-13-oktober-2021-wat-is-nieuw-in-de-norm-nen-10102020). A light circuit counts its loa...

options.label: Pick rooms only (all checked at first).
Select stamps on the plan only.
Rooms, with a switch to use the selected stamps instead.

question: [data model] Does R2 to R7 need a project level above the PDF files (case f)? This replaces D-R2-04, which the user answered B under the old model.

options.label: No. Each file is one document. A riser is one start stamp on each floor. Each floor is routed and sized alone.

question: [data model] Please confirm a change of a rule. Rule 2 of `rules.md` §3 says "connected segments never have different network types". Today a port group joins its ports into one node (`network.ts:102`-`:109`). So a group on a supply port and a return port makes one network, and the network takes the type of the first segment (`network.ts:140`-`:145`, G7). The word "connected" changes meaning if the user agrees: **joined by a segment, or joined by a port group whose segments all have one network type.** Under the new meaning, a group never joins two networks of different types. Rule 2 stays true under the new meaning. The old meaning would make case (d) impossible. The group exists only if the user makes it (G7: the library has none). Which meaning does the user want?

options.label: Accept the new meaning. `computeNetworks` keeps two networks apart when a port group would join different types. The group still joins networks of one type.
Keep the old meaning. The dialog only warns, and the user must not group ports of different types.

reason: a network of one type must not take the type of another, and case (d) needs one network for each start port. The R3 plan changes the union key so that it includes the network type. `solveFlow` builds its graph from `network.segmentIds` only (`flow.ts:57`, `:64`-`:69`), so it should work. This is not verified. The R3 plan lists every consumer of `computeNetworks` and tests each. question: Where does the root of the flow solve come from (G14, G15)?

options.label: The start stamp comes from the user as input. "Size network" (R5) and the route command (R6) pass it as `rootElementId` to `solveFlow`. Nothing is stored. The live flow overlay (`recomputeFlow`, `scene.ts:3005`) keeps the fallback.
Store the start stamp (an optional mark on the stamp, for example a flag), so the overlay also uses it. This is a schema step.

reason: it keeps the model (no stored grouping) and fixes the sizing, which writes data. The overlay is a display only, and a wrong root there is visible and harmless. The fallback stays for a network with one equipment stamp. Core tests: a start port with two segments (degree 2) gives the start stamp as the root when it is passed; a second equipment stamp in the network does not take the root; and the id-prefix case of G15 (`stamp-1` against `stamp-12`).
